nodes.summary: Rounding `c · W` to integers changes the rescaled score of every site by at most `w / (2c)`.
nodes.title: Scaling and rounding error

nodes.summary: The likelihood `∏ₖ q (x k)` of a sequence of length `m` under the background of independent letters with law `q`.
nodes.title: Background likelihood of a sequence

nodes.summary: The Boltzmann PWM `q b e^{-λ ε i b} / Zᵢ` of an energy matrix `ε`.
nodes.title: Boltzmann position weight matrix

nodes.summary: The both-strand score is invariant under reverse complementing the sequence, for an involutive complement.
nodes.title: The both-strand score is invariant under reverse complementing the sequence

nodes.summary: The both-strand score: the larger of the max-pooled responses of `W` and of its reverse complement.
nodes.title: Both-strand convolution score

nodes.summary: The convolution response is the PWM score of the window.
nodes.title: The convolution response is the PWM score of the window

nodes.summary: On a sequence of length `m + w`, its response at window `i ≤ m` is the response of `W` on the reverse complement at window `m - i`.
nodes.title: The reverse-complement filter scans the other strand

nodes.summary: Dropping the first letter shifts the responses by one window.
nodes.title: Translation equivariance

nodes.summary: The response of a convolution (cross-correlation) filter `W` of width `w` on the one-hot encoded sequence `x` at the window starting at `i`: `∑ k, ∑ b, W k b * oneHot (x (i + k)) b`.
nodes.title: Convolution filter response at a window

nodes.summary: Every letter can occur in every motif column: for each column `i` and letter `b` some sequence has `b` at offset `i` of some possible occurrence. This keeps the M-step positive.
nodes.title: Coverage condition for motif columns

nodes.summary: The M-step maximizes the EM objective over PWMs with positive entries and normalized columns: for every `θ'`, `Q(θ' | θ) ≤ Q(mStep θ | θ)` (Gibbs' inequality per column).
nodes.title: The M-step maximizes the EM objective

nodes.summary: Some window attains the max-pooled output.
nodes.title: Max pooling returns the best PWM hit

nodes.summary: Karlin–Altschul `λ` (Karlin and Altschul 1990): if the expected score under a positive background distribution is negative and some score is positive, there is a unique `λ > 0` with `∑ pₐ p_b e^{λ s_{ab}} = 1`.
nodes.title: Karlin–Altschul `λ`

nodes.summary: Under `Covers`, every expected count is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of expected motif counts

nodes.summary: The expected count of letter `b` in motif column `i` under the posteriors at `θ`: `∑ₘ ∑_z P(z | xₘ, θ) [start z = some j ∧ xₘ (j + i) = b]`.
nodes.title: Expected letter counts in motif columns

nodes.summary: For laws `P ≪ Q`, the information content of `P` against `Q` is `KL(P ‖ Q) / log 2`, Mathlib's `klDiv` in bits.
nodes.title: Information content is a Kullback–Leibler divergence

nodes.summary: Information content is nonnegative (Gibbs' inequality) for a column distribution and a positive background distribution.
nodes.title: Information content is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a four-letter alphabet (DNA) and the uniform background, a column carries between `0` and `2` bits.
nodes.title: A DNA column carries at most two bits

nodes.summary: Against the uniform background, a column carries at most `log₂ |α|` bits.
nodes.title: Information content is at most the log of the alphabet size

nodes.summary: Information content against the uniform background (Schneider et al. 1986): `log₂ |α| - H(p)`, the maximal entropy minus the column entropy.
nodes.title: Information content against the uniform background

nodes.summary: The information content `∑_b p b log₂ (p b / q b)` (in bits) of a PWM column `p` against the background `q` (Schneider et al. 1986). Letters with `p b = 0` contribute `0`.
nodes.title: Information content of a position weight matrix column

nodes.summary: Each column of the Boltzmann PWM is a distribution.
nodes.title: Columns of the Boltzmann matrix are distributions

nodes.summary: At a root of `pairMGF p s λ = 1` the target frequencies form a distribution on pairs.
nodes.title: Target frequencies form a distribution on pairs

nodes.summary: Every window's PWM score is at most the max-pooled output.
nodes.title: Every window's PWM score is at most the max-pooled output

nodes.summary: The motif likelihood is nondecreasing along the EM iterates.
nodes.title: The motif likelihood is nondecreasing along the EM iterates

nodes.summary: `log (p i b / q b) = -λ ε i b - log Zᵢ` for the Boltzmann PWM.
nodes.title: Log-odds are affine in the energies

nodes.summary: The log-odds matrix `log (p i b / q b)` of a site model against a background (natural logarithm).
nodes.title: Log-odds matrix of a site model

nodes.summary: The M-step: normalized expected letter counts, `θ' i b = c i b / ∑_{b'} c i b'`.
nodes.title: M-step for position weight matrices

nodes.summary: The responses only read the positions `< m + w` of a sequence of length `m + w`.
nodes.title: Filter responses read only positions within the sequence length

nodes.summary: Max pooling the reverse-complement filter equals max pooling `W` on the reverse complement.
nodes.title: Max pooling the reverse-complement filter equals max pooling `W` on the reverse complement

nodes.summary: Pooling `max (conv + β) 0` over the windows gives `max (maxPool + β) 0`.
nodes.title: Bias and ReLU commute with max pooling

nodes.summary: Global max pooling over the `m + 1` windows of a sequence of length `m + w`.
nodes.title: Global max pooling

nodes.summary: With no occurrence, the joint is the prior times the background likelihood.
nodes.title: Joint likelihood with no motif occurrence

nodes.summary: For a positive background and an occurrence at `j`, the joint is the prior times the product of `θ (k - j)` inside the window and `q` outside.
nodes.title: The joint is the window model

nodes.summary: The joint likelihood of a sequence `x` and a latent occurrence `z` with prior `prior z` and start `start z` (`none`: no occurrence): background letters outside the window, site-model letters inside. One occurrence per sequence (OOPS) is `Z = Fin (n + 1)`, `start = some`, `prior` uniform; zero or one (ZOOPS) is `Z = Option (Fin (n + 1))`, `start = id`, `prior none = 1 - γ` and `prior (some j) = γ / (n + 1)` for a…
nodes.title: Joint likelihood of a sequence and a motif occurrence

nodes.summary: The motif model is positive for a positive background and a positive prior.
nodes.title: Positivity of the motif model

nodes.summary: The motif model as an EM model on `PosPWM`.
nodes.title: Motif model as an EM model

nodes.summary: The one-hot encoding of a letter: `oneHot a b = 1` if `b = a` and `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: One-hot encoding of a letter

nodes.summary: `pValue q M t = ∑_{s : score M s ≥ t} ∏ᵢ q (s i)`, the background probability `P_q(score M ≥ t)` when `q` is a distribution.
nodes.title: Exact p-values

nodes.summary: The exact p-value of the score threshold `t`, summed over the computed distribution.
nodes.title: Exact p-value of a score threshold

nodes.summary: The moment generating function `∑ₐ ∑_b pₐ p_b e^{λ s_{ab}}` of a pair score under independent letters with law `p`.
nodes.title: Moment generating function of a pair score

nodes.summary: The partition function of a positive background is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the column partition function

nodes.summary: The column partition function `Z = ∑_b q b e^{-λ ε b}` of energies `ε` at inverse temperature `λ`.
nodes.title: Column partition function of an energy matrix

nodes.summary: PWMs with positive entries and columns summing to `1`: the EM parameter space.
nodes.title: Positive position weight matrices

nodes.summary: The posterior of the occurrence `z` is proportional to its prior times the likelihood ratio of its window (Lawrence and Reilly 1990; Bailey and Elkan 1995).
nodes.title: The E-step in closed form

nodes.summary: The reverse-complement filter: `rcFilter W k b = W (Fin.rev k) (comp b)`.
nodes.title: Reverse-complement filter

nodes.summary: The reverse complement of the length-`L` prefix of `x`: position `j < L` holds the complement of `x (L - 1 - j)`.
nodes.title: Reverse complement of a sequence prefix

nodes.summary: The relative entropy of the target frequencies (Altschul 1991): `λ ∑ q_{ab} s_{ab} = ∑ q_{ab} log (q_{ab} / (pₐ p_b))`, which is nonnegative.
nodes.title: The relative entropy of the target frequencies

nodes.summary: `scoreDist q M t` is `∑_{s : score M s = t} ∏ᵢ q (s i)`, for every `q`. When `q` is a distribution this is the background probability of the score `t` (the weights sum to `1` by `sum_bgLik`).
nodes.title: The column recursion computes the exact score distribution

nodes.summary: The background distribution of the score of an integer matrix `M`, computed column by column from the point mass at `0` (Staden 1989; Touzet and Varré 2007).
nodes.title: Background score distribution of an integer matrix

nodes.summary: Every such score matrix is a log-odds matrix (Karlin and Altschul 1990): `s_{ab} = log (q_{ab} / (pₐ p_b)) / λ` for every `λ > 0`; at the Karlin–Altschul root the `q_{ab}` form a distribution (`isDist_targetFreq`), the implicit target frequencies.
nodes.title: Every such score matrix is a log-odds matrix

nodes.summary: The log-odds score of a selected site is `-λ E(s)` up to the constant `∑ᵢ log Zᵢ`.
nodes.title: Log-odds score of a selected site is its scaled energy up to a constant

nodes.summary: The log-odds score is a log-likelihood ratio (Staden 1989; Stormo 2000): for positive site model and background, `score (logOdds p q) s = log (siteLik p s / bgLik q s)`.
nodes.title: The log-odds score is a log-likelihood ratio

nodes.summary: One column of the score-distribution recursion: from the distribution `d` of the score of the first columns, the distribution after adding a column `c` with background `q`, `∑_b q b · (d shifted by c b)`.
nodes.title: One column step of the score-distribution recursion

nodes.summary: The score `∑ᵢ W i (s i)` of a site `s` of width `w` under a position weight matrix `W`.
nodes.title: Score of a site under a position weight matrix

nodes.summary: Boltzmann selection of background sites with an additive energy yields the product site model with columns `boltzmannPWM`. This is an identity for every `q` (both sides vanish when some `Zᵢ = 0`); it is a statement about laws for positive `q`.
nodes.title: Berg–von Hippel

nodes.summary: The law of background sites selected with weight `e^{-λ E(s)}` for the additive energy `E s = score ε s = ∑ᵢ ε i (s i)`: `q(s) e^{-λ E(s)} / ∑_{s'} q(s') e^{-λ E(s')}`.
nodes.title: Law of energy-selected background sites

nodes.summary: The likelihood `∏ᵢ p i (s i)` of a site under the product (column-independent) site model `p`.
nodes.title: Site likelihood under a column-independent model

nodes.summary: The position `j + i` of motif column `i` for a motif starting at `j`, in a sequence of length `n + w` (so `n + 1` possible starts).
nodes.title: Sequence position of a motif column

nodes.summary: The background law of independent letters is a distribution on sequences.
nodes.title: Background likelihoods form a distribution

nodes.summary: Thresholding the log-odds score is most powerful (Neyman–Pearson): a test `φ` of the background (null) against the site model whose background size is at most that of the threshold test `score > t` has at most its power.
nodes.title: Thresholding the log-odds score is most powerful

nodes.summary: Under the site model, `E[score] = log 2 · ∑ᵢ IC(pᵢ ‖ q)`. This is an identity for every `q` (both sides use the same logarithms); it is an expected log-likelihood ratio for a positive background.
nodes.title: The expected log-odds score is the total information content

nodes.summary: A product of column distributions is a distribution on sites.
nodes.title: Product site likelihoods form a distribution

nodes.summary: At the Karlin–Altschul root `λ > 0`, the expected score `∑ q_{ab} s_{ab}` under the target frequencies is positive.
nodes.title: The target score is positive

nodes.summary: The implicit target frequencies `q_{ab} = pₐ p_b e^{λ s_{ab}}` of a score matrix.
nodes.title: Implicit target frequencies of a score matrix

nodes.summary: The window of length `w` of `x` starting at `i`.
nodes.title: Window of a sequence starting at a position

nodes.summary: The likelihood ratio of the window at `j` under the site model `θ` against the background `q`, and `1` when there is no motif occurrence.
nodes.title: Likelihood ratio of a motif window

nodes.summary: The window of width `w` of `x` starting at `j`.
nodes.title: Window of a sequence at a given start

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
